root_cause: When a focused element is removed from the DOM, the MutationObserver callback `checkDomRemoval` calls `tryFocus(getInitialFocusNode())` to restore focus, but the internal tabbable node cache (`state.tabbableGroups`) is stale. `getInitialFocusNode()` relies on `state.tabbableGroups[0].firstTabbableNode` which still references the removed node, causing focus restoration to fail and focus to fall back to the body element.
repair_strategy: Refresh the tabbable node cache by calling `updateTabbableNodes()` before attempting focus restoration in `checkDomRemoval`, ensuring `getInitialFocusNode()` can locate the new first tabbable node in the dialog.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains trapped inside the basket dialog after removing the row containing the focused button, preventing focus loss to the page body and maintaining WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order) conformance for modal dialogs.
functional_risks: Minimal: updateTabbableNodes() is idempotent and already called during activation/unpause; adding it here synchronizes cache with DOM after mutation.
verification_requirements: Run the provided journey: open dialog, Tab to first remove button, Enter to remove row, verify #basket:focus-within is true and #count reads '2 items'.
Verify Shift+Tab from first tabbable node wraps to last tabbable node inside dialog (regression guard).
